question.problem:
The random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{16}xy,\, & 0\le x\le 2,\,\,0\le y\le 4, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

If $\text{E}[X]=\frac{4}{3}$ and $\text{E}[Y]=\frac{8}{3},$ find the covariance matrix for $X$ and $Y.$
question.worked_solution:
For two random variables $X$ and $Y,$ the covariance matrix $Σ$ is given by

$$
Σ=[\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & \text{Cov}[X,Y] \\ \text{Cov}[Y,X] & \text{Var}[Y]\end{aligned}].
$$

Recall that the variance of a random variable $X$ is determined by the formula

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}.
$$

We compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}]$ using the rule of the lazy statistician:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{0}^{2}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{0}^{2}{x}^{2}(\frac{1}{16}xy)\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{16}{\int }_{0}^{4}y{\int }_{0}^{2}{x}^{3}\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{16}{\int }_{0}^{4}y\cdot {[\frac{1}{4}{x}^{4}]}_{0}^{2}\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{0}^{4}y\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot {[\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}]}_{0}^{4} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot 8 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =2-{(\frac{4}{3})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{2}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, we compute $\text{E}[{Y}^{2}]$ using the rule of the lazy statistician:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{Y}^{2}] & ={\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{0}^{2}{y}^{2}\cdot f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{0}^{2}{y}^{2}(\frac{1}{16}xy)\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{16}{\int }_{0}^{4}{y}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}x\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{16}{\int }_{0}^{4}{y}^{3}{[\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}]}_{0}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{8}{\int }_{0}^{4}{y}^{3}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{8}\cdot {[\frac{1}{4}{y}^{4}]}_{0}^{4} \\  & =\frac{1}{8}\cdot 64 \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[Y] & =\text{E}[{Y}^{2}]-\text{E}[Y]^{2} \\  & =8-{(\frac{8}{3})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{8}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the covariance of $X$ and $Y.$ The joint support of $X$ and $Y$ is given by the rectangle

$$
S=[0,2]\times [0,4].
$$

Moreover, we can write

$$
f(x,y)=g(x)\cdot h(y),
$$

where $g(x)=\frac{x}{2}$ and $h(y)=\frac{y}{8}.$

Hence, $X$ and $Y$ are independent, and consequently $\text{Cov}[X,Y]=0.$

Therefore, the covariance matrix is given by

$$
Σ=[\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & \text{Cov}[X,Y] \\ \text{Cov}[Y,X] & \text{Var}[Y]\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{9} & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{8}{9}\end{aligned}].
$$
